raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #47245.

`reset_for_retract` keeps a request's `output_ids`, and the re-prefill feeds them back as input. But `prepare_for_extend` builds a fresh `BatchedPenalizerOrchestrator`, so the request's frequency, presence and repetition rows start at zero and its `min_new_tokens` counter restarts at 0. From the retraction point on, the request is penalized as if it had generated nothing. Its output then diverges from an uninterrupted run with no error, and a `min_new_tokens` request can be held past its minimum.

## Modifications

- `penaltylib/orchestrator.py`: add `BatchedPenalizerOrchestrator.cumulate_output_history(rows, output_ids)`. It pads the histories with `vocab_size` and passes them to each prepared penalizer through a new `_cumulate_output_history` hook.
- Frequency, presence and repetition penalizers scatter the history into their rows. Frequency uses `scatter_add_` and the other two use `scatter_`, matching their per-step `_cumulate_output_tokens`. The padding column is dropped. `min_new_tokens` adds the history length to `len_output_tokens`.
- `ScheduleBatch.prepare_for_extend`: after building `sampling_info`, replay `output_ids` for requests that have them when a penalizer is active. For a normal first prefill `output_ids` is empty, so nothing changes. dLLM batches are skipped because they re-extend with `output_ids` on every block and don't sample through penaltylib.

Scope: this covers the regular re-prefill path. The PD decode-side prebuilt path (`prepare_for_prebuilt`) also builds a fresh orchestrator for retracted requests and could get the same treatment in a follow-up. I left it alone because I can't test PD here.

## Accuracy Tests

New `TestCumulateOutputHistory` cases in `test/registered/unit/sampling/test_penaltylib.py`:
- Replaying histories (including repeats) into some rows of a batch with all four penalizers gives the same additive and scaling penalties as cumulating the tokens one step at a time, and rows without history stay untouched.
- Retained tokens count toward `min_new_tokens`, so EOS is unmasked once the minimum is reached.

```
python -m pytest test/registered/unit/sampling/test_penaltylib.py test/registered/unit/sampling/test_sampling_metadata_staging.py -q
48 passed, 2 skipped
```

`pre-commit run` on the changed files passes. I ran CPU-only unit tests. I didn't run a server or the issue's end-to-end retraction repro, and I didn't test on GPU.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No hot-path change: the replay only runs during prefill for requests that already have `output_ids` (retracted requests) and only when a penalizer is active.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

+    def cumulate_output_history(self, rows: List[int], output_ids: List[Sequence[int]]):
+        """
+        Replay already generated tokens into freshly prepared penalizer rows.
+
+        A retracted request keeps its ``output_ids`` but is re-prefilled with a
+        new orchestrator, so its rows start from zero. Replaying the history
+        gives the same state as feeding ``output_ids[i]`` one token at a time
+        through ``cumulate_output_tokens``.
+
+        Args:
+            rows: Batch row of each request to replay.
+            output_ids: Tokens to replay for each entry of ``rows``.
+        """
+        if not self.is_required:
+            return
+        keep = [(row, ids) for row, ids in zip(rows, output_ids) if len(ids) > 0]
+        if not keep:
+            return
+
+        # Pad with vocab_size: penalizers scatter into a vocab_size + 1 wide
+        # buffer and drop the padding column.
+        padded = torch.nn.utils.rnn.pad_sequence(
+            [torch.tensor(list(ids), dtype=torch.int64) for _, ids in keep],
+            batch_first=True,
+            padding_value=self.vocab_size,
+        ).to(self.device, non_blocking=True)
+        row_indices = torch.tensor(
+            [row for row, _ in keep], dtype=torch.int64, device=self.device
+        )
+        for penalizer in self.penalizers.values():
+            penalizer.cumulate_output_history(row_indices, padded)

     def apply(self, logits: torch.Tensor, repeat: Optional[int] = None):

+def _scatter_history(
+    rows_values: torch.Tensor,
+    output_ids: torch.Tensor,
+    src: torch.Tensor,

+    """Scatter ``src`` at ``output_ids`` (padded with vocab_size) into a copy of

@@ -526,5 +529,72 @@ def test_merge_one_required(self):
         self.assertEqual(pen.frequency_penalties.shape[0], 2)
 
 
+# Replaying a retained output history (retracted request re-prefill)
+ALL_PENALIZERS = {
+    BatchedFrequencyPenalizer,
+    BatchedMinNewTokensPenalizer,
+    BatchedPresencePenalizer,
+    BatchedRepetitionPenalizer,
+}
+
+
+def _make_penalized_req():
+    req = _make_req(freq=0.5, presence=0.25, min_tokens=6)
+    req.sampling_params.repetition_penalty = 1.5
+    return req
+
+
+class TestCumulateOutputHistory(CustomTestCase):
+    def _penalties(self, orch, batch_size):
+        # Read additive and scaling penalties separately: apply() would run the
+        # torch.compile'd repetition kernel, which needs a C++ toolchain on CPU.
+        additive = torch.zeros(batch_size, VOCAB_SIZE)
+        orch.accumulate_additive_penalties(additive)
+        return additive, orch.accumulate_scaling_penalties()
+
+    def test_history_matches_step_by_step_cumulation(self):
+        """Replaying output_ids into a fresh orchestrator gives the same penalties
+        as cumulating them one decode step at a time."""
+        histories = [[5, 7, 5, 9], [], [3, 3, 3]]
+        reqs = [_make_penalized_req() for _ in histories]
+        orch = BatchedPenalizerOrchestrator(
+            VOCAB_SIZE, _make_batch(reqs), ALL_PENALIZERS
+        )
+        orch.cumulate_output_history(
+            rows=[0, 2], output_ids=[histories[0], histories[2]]
+        )
+        replayed_additive, replayed_scaling = self._penalties(orch, len(reqs))
+
+        for row, history in enumerate(histories):
+            single = BatchedPenalizerOrchestrator(
+                VOCAB_SIZE, _make_batch([_make_penalized_req()]), ALL_PENALIZERS
+            )
+            for token in history:
+                single.cumulate_output_tokens(torch.tensor([token]))
+            additive, scaling = self._penalties(single, 1)
+            torch.testing.assert_close(replayed_additive[row : row + 1], additive)
+            torch.testing.assert_close(replayed_scaling[row : row + 1], scaling)
+
+    def test_history_counts_toward_min_new_tokens(self):
+        """Retained tokens count toward min_new_tokens after a re-prefill."""
+        reqs = [_make_req(min_tokens=3, eos_id=2)]
+        orch = BatchedPenalizerOrchestrator(
+            VOCAB_SIZE, _make_batch(reqs), {BatchedMinNewTokensPenalizer}
+        )
+        orch.cumulate_output_history(rows=[0], output_ids=[[5, 6, 7]])
+        logits = torch.zeros(1, VOCAB_SIZE)
+        orch.apply(logits)
+        self.assertEqual(logits[0, 2].item(), 0.0)
+
+    def test_history_not_required_is_noop(self):
+        """No penalizer is prepared, so replaying a history does nothing."""
+        reqs = [_make_req()]
+        orch = BatchedPenalizerOrchestrator(
+            VOCAB_SIZE, _make_batch(reqs), {BatchedFrequencyPenalizer}
+        )
+        orch.cumulate_output_history(rows=[0], output_ids=[[1, 2]])
+        self.assertFalse(orch.is_required)
+
+
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     unittest.main()
